guards.what: G9: enemy intents are rolled at the end of each monster's own move, not in one pass at the start of the player's turn
guards.issue: MECHANISM: CombatManager.cs:478-484 rolls EVERY enemy's next move in one pass at the start of the player's turn, unconditionally and in enemy-list order, and skips the pass entirely on an extra player turn; the very first roll happens even earlier, in AfterCreatureAdded (CombatManager.cs:860-867). The sim instead advances each monster's own machine as part of performing its move, with telegraph_next_move (monsters/base.py:96-105) as the explicit stand-in, and combat.py:314-329 documents the consequence in the engine itself: a monster stunned this round keeps its move (correct) but MISSES ONE MonsterAi draw where the game takes one. LIVE under seed parity, and the differing draw count is now DEMONSTRATED BY EXECUTION rather than argued (the fix pass's requirement): with a one-LeafSlimeS encounter (monsters/overgrowth/slimes.py:17-56, whose telegraph_next_move draws exactly one weighted_branch_pick on combat_rng.monster_ai on every transition) and a counting proxy installed over the monster_ai accessor, one _run_enemy_turns records `normal enemy turn: MonsterAi draws = 1` and `STUNNED enemy turn: MonsterAi draws = 0`. C# takes 1 in BOTH cases, because PrepareForNextTurn -> RollMove runs for every enemy at player-turn-start regardless of whether it acted (CombatManager.cs:478-484; MonsterModel.cs:415-418). So one stunned enemy round desyncs the MonsterAi stream by exactly one draw, and every later draw in the combat shifts. The stun is player-reachable, not monster-only: Whistle is a ported Ancient Attack card from Tanx's Whistle (cards/whistle.py:30-38) that calls CreatureCmd.stun with no next_move_key, i.e. with no compensating pre-roll (cmds.py:208-218). Dormant under legacy RNG (one shared stream, nothing compares counts). Cross-referenced to Task 10 (monster_state_machine), which owns WHAT the roll returns; if Task 10 finds the sim's roll produces the wrong move, that is Task 10's finding and should cross-reference G9 rather than re-verdict it. Not pinned here: the observable is an RNG-stream draw count, not a hook order, and the conformance suite is its natural home.

guards.what: G10: the combat-end path collapses five C# distinctions into one hook, and the sim's two player-death exits disagree with each other
guards.issue: MECHANISM: C# distinguishes (a) a LOSS -- LoseCombat() -> _pendingLoss -> ProcessPendingLoss(), which fires the CombatEnded C# event and NO HOOK AT ALL (CombatManager.cs:945-965) -- from (b) a VICTORY, which runs EndCombatInternal with ReviveBeforeCombatEnd() -> Hook.AfterCombatEnd -> Hook.AfterCombatVictory (970-1033); and it consults Hook.ShouldStopCombatFromEnding inside IsEnding (196-199). The sim has one _end_combat(player_won) firing one on_combat_end(player_won) (combat.py:347-350), no revive step, and no should_stop_combat_from_ending hook. On top of that, _run_enemy_turns has TWO player-death exits that behave differently: combat.py:308-310 calls _end_combat(player_won=False) (hook fires) while combat.py:332-335 sets phase/result by hand and returns (hook does not). OBSERVED (re-executed in the fix pass, not inherited): `killed from on_enemy_turn_start: hooks=[('on_combat_end', False)]  phase=Phase.COMBAT_OVER  player_dead=True` versus `killed by the attack: hooks=[]  phase=Phase.COMBAT_OVER  player_dead=True` -- same end state, different hook record. DORMANT, and the dormancy evidence was re-executed too: `grep -rn --include=*.py 'def on_combat_end' sts2_rl/` returns the hooks.py:271 dispatcher plus exactly four listeners, and reading all four confirms each gates on victory or on the player being alive -- black_blood.py:18 `if player_won and not self.player.is_dead`, burning_blood.py:16 the same, meat_on_the_bone.py:18 `if not player_won or self.player.is_dead: return`, chosen_cheese.py:20 `if self.player.is_dead: return`. So neither the extra loss-side call nor the missing one changes anything today; and the two ported effects that need ShouldStopCombatFromEnding hand-roll around it (SteamEruptionPower prevents the death instead, powers.py:2004-2010; StockPower spawns the replacement Axebot from on_death, powers.py:2962-2984, which runs before the _all_enemies_dead() check). It goes live for any AfterCombatVictory-only listener with an unconditional effect, and the two-exit inconsistency is live the moment any on_combat_end listener has an effect that outlives the combat.

guards.what: G16: on_hand_emptied is fired from the end-of-turn flush -- the one site C# deliberately excludes -- and from nowhere else

guards.what: G17: Joss Paper's port uses `card.is_ethereal` as its causedByEthereal proxy, so ANY mid-turn exhaust of an Ethereal card is deferred to the flush; C# defers only the turn-end ethereal path
guards.issue: MECHANISM: C#'s AfterCardExhausted takes the CAUSE as a parameter -- `AfterCardExhausted(ctx, card, bool causedByEthereal)` (JossPaper.cs:102-114, dispatched from CardCmd.cs:237-244 / Hook.cs:237-242) -- and `causedByEthereal: true` is passed from exactly TWO sites in the whole decompiled game, both at turn end: CombatManager.cs:1240 (step 53's ethereal exhaust pass) and CardModel.cs:1692 (step 54's OnTurnEndInHandWrapper). Every other Exhaust passes false, including the play-time exhaust of an Exhaust-keyword card at CardModel.cs:1985 (`causedByEthereal: false`). The sim has no cause parameter: relics/joss_paper.py:36 branches on `card.is_ethereal`, a property of the CARD, so an Ethereal card exhausted in the middle of the play phase is booked to _ethereal_pending and its credit is withheld until on_hand_emptied fires from the flush. LIVE, both sides ported and obtainable, and verified by execution. Trigger: Apparition (cards/apparition.py:12-38) is a ported 1-cost Ancient Skill with `exhausts = True` AND `is_ethereal = True`, granted by the ported relic Distinguished Cape (relics/distinguished_cape.py); Joss Paper is a ported Uncommon relic. OBSERVED: with [joss_paper], four plain Strikes exhausted first (cards_exhausted = 4, ethereal_pending = 0) and then Apparition played, the sim records cards_exhausted = 4, ethereal_pending = 1 and hand 1 -> 0 -- NO draw. C# treats that exhaust as the fifth non-ethereal one (causedByEthereal false), fires DrawIfThresholdMet immediately and hands the player a card they can still play this turn (hand 1 -> 1). Knock-on at turn end: the sim credits the deferred exhaust inside discard_hand, AFTER the flush, so its drawn card survives into the next turn -- next hand 6 -- where C#'s mid-turn draw was flushed with the rest and the next hand is 5. Distinct from G4 (there the credit is stranded because the flush is skipped; here it is merely late) but the same port, and the same one-line fix does not cover both. Pinned: test_hook_order.py::TestTurnStructureOrder::test_joss_paper_credits_a_mid_turn_ethereal_exhaust_at_once.

guards.what: G18: Pael's Eye's AnyCardsPlayedThisTurn predicate is missing BOTH of its C# clauses -- the turn-1 Whispering Earring short-circuit and the auto-play exclusion
guards.issue: MECHANISM: PaelsEye.AnyCardsPlayedThisTurn (PaelsEye.cs:149-156) has two clauses the sim's relics/paels_eye.py:27-34 has neither of. (1) PaelsEye.cs:152 -- `if (playerCombatState.TurnNumber == 1 && Owner.Relics.Any(r => r is WhisperingEarring)) return true;` -- on turn 1, merely HOLDING Whispering Earring counts as having played, which switches Pael's Eye off for that turn. (2) PaelsEye.cs:155 -- the history scan filters `&& !e.CardPlay.IsAutoPlay`, so auto-plays never count. The sim's predicate is a bare `any(history.of_type(CardPlayedEntry, this_turn=True))`: history.py:80-81 records a CardPlayedEntry from on_card_played for EVERY play including auto-plays (combat.auto_play at combat.py:424-439 goes through _resolve_card_play, and relics/whispering_earring.py:36 says the missing auto flag is a known divergence). The two omissions CANCEL in the common case -- Whispering Earring's turn-1 auto-plays are counted by the sim and so reproduce clause (1)'s effect -- and diverge otherwise. LIVE, verified by execution on both legs. Leg (2), reachability proven with two ported relics and no exotic deck: with relics=[paels_eye] and a 9-Strike + 1-Imbued-Defend deck (Imbued is granted by the ported relic Electric Shrymp, relics/electric_shrymp.py:17-21), on seeds 0, 4 and 5 the Imbued card lands in the opening hand and auto-plays, and the sim reports _any_cards_played_this_turn = True and should_take_extra_turn = FALSE where C# reports False and TRUE. Isolated from G14's draw ordering, the same thing shows with a direct `cs.auto_play(card)` on turn 1: sim _any_cards_played_this_turn = True, should_take_extra_turn = False; C# would grant the extra turn. Leg (1), the clause named in the review: with relics=[whispering_earring, paels_eye] and an opening hand in which nothing is playable (a 10-Dazed deck; valid card actions = []), the Earring's loop plays nothing, and the sim reports _any_cards_played_this_turn = False and should_take_extra_turn = TRUE where C#'s clause makes it False -- i.e. the sim hands out a Pael's Eye extra turn (plus its hand exhaust) that the real game withholds. Leg (1) needs a turn-1 hand with no playable card, which is constructible but I could not name a realistic Ironclad deck for it, so the LIVE label rests on leg (2). Pinned on leg (2), which is the reachability-proven one: test_hook_order.py::TestTurnStructureOrder::test_paels_eye_ignores_auto_plays. Adjacent to G3 (which owns WHEN the extra-turn predicate is evaluated); this guard owns WHAT it reads.
